newsitem.title: JAPAN: NISSAN MOTOR SAYS DEVELOPS ALUMINIUM CAR BODY.
newsitem.headline: NISSAN MOTOR SAYS DEVELOPS ALUMINIUM CAR BODY.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it had developed a car body made out of aluminium, and expected it to be commercialised by 2000.
"We plan to commercialise the technology by 2000, but we are still experimenting how many types of vehicles the technology can be used in," a Nissan spokeswoman said.
"Production costs are expected to rise (compared with steel) and we will have to make alterations in our plants if we are to use this method," she added.
The spokeswoman also said the company had not yet decided how much aluminium was needed to make a single car as the technology was still in the experimental stage.
Compared with conventional steel bodies, the new body is made of light and highly malleable aluminium pipes, Nissan said in a statement.
The technology allows the weight of a car body to be cut by 40 percent while doubling its rigidity, it said.
